An Apple billboard featuring a child holding an iPhone has drawn criticism in Italy, prompting the country's child rights watchdog to refer the advertisement to three regulatory bodies. Here's what happened.

Apple's "Relax, it's iPhone" ad campaign has sparked controversy in Italy

Italy's child and adolescent rights authority AGIA has raised concerns over an Apple billboard in Milan. The billboard features a child holding an iPhone, accompanied by the Italian tagline "Tutto ok, è iPhone" ("It's all good, it's an iPhone").

The ad is part of Apple's long-running "Relax, it's iPhone" series, which typically depicts iPhones surviving potentially damaging situations.

Recent billboards in the series have shown iPhones being used in heavy rain, knocked off a table by a kitten, and carried away by a dog.

One of the new billboards features a child holding an iPhone, seemingly conveying that parents need not worry if their child drops the device. However, AGIA has labelled it as normalising the "electronic babysitter" phenomenon, sparking controversy.

AGIA said in a press release that the matter was brought to their attention by a Milan resident, who found the image "disturbing" because it "brought together two worlds that should remain separate."

AGIA said it has referred the case to Italy's communications regulator AGCOM, the Italian competition authority AGCM, and the country's advertising self-regulatory body IAP, "for appropriate review and any possible action."

Apple has not publicly responded to the matter as of yet.
